themes.theme: 1. Typography foundation: a text face for reading, the display face only for page titles, a type scale and highlighted code
2. One brand in two modes: colour roles, surfaces lighter than the page, status tokens and a contrast check in CI
3. Theme mechanics and the theme control: no flash, color-scheme, print, OS preference, and one control that is reachable on every page and device
4. Landing page rebuild: header, honest server-rendered hero, a real visual, proof strip, one primary action, compact routes
5. One navigation model: a single {href,label} config, one name, tier and practice hierarchy, wider search, footer and breadcrumbs that agree
6. Page shell primitives: PageShell, PageHeader, unboxed Prose, Card and Badge, applied to every page type
7. Wayfinding inside very long lessons (40,000-70,000 px pages)
8. Reliability, mobile and accessibility defects that block use

conflicts.between: theme-1 / layout-3 / design-critic-1 / landing-13 (Inter for text, Cal Sans kept as display) vs unslop direction A (IBM Plex Sans, remove Cal Sans); and layout-5 + theme proposal (display face on lesson h2) vs design-critic-1 (h1 only)
conflicts.issue: All lenses agree body text must leave Cal Sans, but they disagree on which text face and on where the display face may still appear.
conflicts.recommendation: Ship Inter now, since it is already self-hosted (add 500/600 or the variable woff2). It fixes the P1 with no new font family. Keep Cal Sans only for the landing H1, page H1s and the wordmark. Lesson H2s use Inter semibold, and the layer break comes from the rule and spacing in layout-5. Reason: lesson H2s are long and numerous, and Cal Sans has one weight. Plex is a taste call with no learner gain that justifies a new download. Revisit it only if the brand direction (next conflict) is redone.

conflicts.between: theme proposal / design-critic-3 (ship Light and Dark only, retire ocean/sunset/forest/violet) vs unslop (keep all ten theme ids as accent swaps over a shared ramp); theme-5 vs responsive-a11y-7 (different forest-dark --primary values)
conflicts.issue: Two opposite decisions on the number of themes. The forest-dark contrast fix is written twice with different values (161 94% 40% vs 161 84% 40%).
conflicts.recommendation: Keep two themes, default-light and default-dark. ThemeProvider maps any stored '<palette>-light' or '<palette>-dark' value to the matching mode, which keeps saved preferences working (unslop's reason for keeping the ids). Reason: each palette is another set of AA pairs to check across about 118 interactives, and today they recolour only 4-5 variables. With two themes the forest-dark fix is moot. If the owner keeps one accent swap, its values must pass the CI contrast check from theme-9, whichever number that gives.

conflicts.between: theme-3 / design-critic-2 / layout-7 (keep navy and cyan, mint for highlights or progress) vs unslop (graphite neutral #131418, sky accent, retire mint and navy, off-white hero button) vs default-light values (theme: white + 192 85% 30%; design-critic: cool white + cyan-700; unslop: #f8f8f7 + #0a6c9e)
conflicts.issue: Three palettes are proposed for the same 'one brand in two modes' goal, and they disagree on mint and on the primary button fill.
conflicts.recommendation: Keep a navy-tinted slate neutral: it is the existing identity, and the always-dark code and figure panels (slate-950) already sit on it. Adopt the structural rules all three share: near-white text, surfaces lighter than the page in dark, one interactive hue (cyan) as a solid fill without the gradient, and status roles. Retire mint as a UI colour. Progress and pass use the new --success role. Reason: two cyan-like hues side by side are the root of the confusion. One person (the theme lens owner) sets the exact HSL values with the contrast script, so layout-7 and theme-3 are not done twice.

conflicts.between: theme-8 (P3, System optional) vs responsive-a11y-v2 (P2, follow the OS) vs unslop and design-critic ('dark stays the default')
conflicts.issue: Should a first-time visitor get dark or follow the device setting?
conflicts.recommendation: Follow prefers-color-scheme and fall back to dark when the device states no preference. Do it as part of the two-theme consolidation, when next-themes' value map is cheap. Reason: dark stays the default for most developers, whose devices are dark, and light-mode learners stop landing in the wrong mode. Treat it as P2 bundled with theme-6, not as a separate task.

conflicts.between: design-critic-3 (remove the theme select from the Navbar, keep only a toggle) vs navigation-6 / responsive-a11y-3 (add the full ThemeSwitcher to the phone menu) vs landing-7 / navigation-2 / responsive-a11y-9 (theme toggle in a new public header) vs theme-16 (one menu button: Light, Dark, System)
conflicts.issue: Four lenses each specify a different theme control for a different place.
conflicts.recommendation: Build theme-16's single menu button (Light, Dark, System as menuitemradio, 40-44 px target) and use that one component in the desktop navbar, the phone menu's Appearance row and the PublicHeader. Any palette options, if kept, live only in /settings. Reason: one component, one test and the same behaviour everywhere.

conflicts.between: navigation proposal (Practice disclosure containing Labs) vs navigation-8 (drop wideOnly so Labs is a top-level link at every width) vs header link sets for the landing page (landing-7: Curriculum, Labs, Practice, Interview prep; navigation-2: Curriculum, Practice, Interview prep; design-critic-5: Curriculum, Practice, Labs, Dashboard; responsive-a11y-9: three links)
conflicts.issue: There is no agreed top-level navigation, and the landing header lists differ in every proposal.
conflicts.recommendation: Use one config in site-links.ts. Learning navbar: Curriculum, Practice (a disclosure with Hub, Labs, Exercises, Interactive models, Waveform Studio), Interview prep, Reference (a disclosure), Dashboard. No 'Start here' and no separate Labs item. Mark Practice and Labs current on /practice/lab/*. PublicHeader: the first three items from the same config, plus search, the theme control and 'Start learning' or 'Continue'. Reason: labs already live under /practice. Five items fit from 1024 px without 'More'. The landing page needs focus, not the full map, and the footer carries the rest.

conflicts.between: layout-15 / design-critic-19 / navigation-11 (xl:hidden on the outline quick links) vs responsive-a11y-12 (show only the links the navbar hides between lg and xl) vs navigation-8 (which changes what the navbar hides)
conflicts.issue: These fixes depend on each other. Whatever navigation-8 does decides which quick links are still needed.
conflicts.recommendation: Land the navigation config first. With five items visible from lg, delete the quick links from the docked outline at every width and keep them only in the phone drawer. Reason: it removes the duplicate entirely, rather than tuning it per breakpoint twice.

conflicts.between: navigation-11 (merge the outline and the main menu into one phone hamburger drawer) vs responsive-a11y-14 (keep two buttons, add a 'Course outline' row to the menu and an optional label)
conflicts.issue: These are two different phone header designs.
conflicts.recommendation: Do responsive-a11y-14 now (S), together with the Appearance and Settings rows from navigation-6. Revisit the merge only after the outline is used more on phones. Reason: the merge rewrites both dialogs and their focus traps (which responsive-a11y says work today), the Ctrl+B outline model and mobile-navigation.spec.ts. The labelled button and the menu row fix discoverability at a fraction of the risk.

conflicts.between: landing-3 / design-critic-6 (a static SVG poster or crop in the hero, one interactive lazy-mounted below the fold) vs unslop (hero built from live parts: RegionLadder, StepWaveform, CodeTrace, simulateTimeSlot) vs landing-1 / design-critic-10 (the hero must render with no JS and no opacity-0)
conflicts.issue: A live hero visual needs client JS in the very part of the page that must be server-rendered and visible at once.
conflicts.recommendation: Put a server-rendered static SVG in the hero (it can be produced from the same RegionLadder data at build time) that links to the live interactive. Lazy-mount one real interactive below the fold. Reason: this keeps LCP and no-JS rendering (landing-1) and still shows the real thing one scroll down.

conflicts.between: landing proposal step 7 (add an M0-M8 milestone teaser) vs unslop (do not add the ladder to the landing page) vs layout-9 (move the milestone ladder lower on /curriculum) vs landing-19 (mobile page already about 7 screens)
conflicts.issue: These disagree on whether the milestone ladder belongs on the landing page.
conflicts.recommendation: Do not add a section. Put one line in the compact route strip, such as 'Builds toward M0 to M8: from a self-checking testbench to …', linking to /curriculum#routes. Reason: the landing page must get shorter (landing-19), and the ladder's full form stays on /curriculum.

conflicts.between: landing-1 / design-critic-10 (no entrance motion, drop framer-motion) vs unslop (one hero entrance: opacity plus an 8px rise over 400ms)
conflicts.issue: These disagree on whether the hero may animate in.
conflicts.recommendation: Render the hero static. If any entrance is wanted, use a CSS motion-safe keyframe of 200ms or less, with no framer-motion and no JS-gated opacity. Reason: CSS animations still finish without JS, and a reduced-motion user sees nothing move.

conflicts.between: navigation-v1 / responsive-a11y-4 (sticky 'On this page: <section>' bar below xl) vs layout-11 (a reading-progress bar under the header)
conflicts.issue: Two sticky strips would stack under the 64 px header on phones and eat reading space.
conflicts.recommendation: Build one 44 px sticky bar that shows the current section, opens the TOC sheet and draws reading progress as a thin line on its bottom edge. On xl, show only the progress line. Reason: one component, one test and minimal lost height.

conflicts.between: theme-11 (delete ui/CodeBlock.tsx when adding rehype-pretty-code) vs gap-1 (long listings need copy and collapse)
conflicts.issue: CodeBlock.tsx holds the only copy-to-clipboard code in the repo, and theme-11 deletes it.
conflicts.recommendation: Add a pre override for the highlighted output that has a language label, a copy button and the gap-1 collapse, and port the clipboard logic from CodeBlock.tsx before deleting it. Do both in the same change.

conflicts.between: layout-4 (68ch) vs theme-10 (70ch) vs design-critic-9 (72ch) vs unslop (about 70ch); design-critic-16 (back link only below sm) vs layout-12 / navigation-10 (one chevron trail everywhere)
conflicts.issue: Several near-duplicate specifications that different people could implement twice.
conflicts.recommendation: Use 68ch in the single Prose config from layout's proposal. Build one Breadcrumbs component that takes {label, href}[] and collapses to a parent back link below sm. Give one owner each, so the measure and the breadcrumb are written once.

gaps.title: Full code listings render fully expanded: a single block reaches 18,600 px, with no collapse, label or copy button
gaps.where: Lesson code fences in 61 lesson files (blocks of 120+ lines), worst in B-AXI-6, A-UVM-8, A-UVM-7, A-UVM-6 and A-UVM-4B sub-pages
gaps.evidence: Python scan of content/curriculum/**/*.mdx: 65 fenced blocks of 120+ lines in 61 files, and 32 of 200+ lines. The longest are B-AXI-6_AXI_Verification_Performance/index.mdx:883 (775 lines), A-UVM-8/index.mdx:836 (692), A-UVM-7/index.mdx:1063 (659) and A-UVM-4B/explicit-vs-implicit.mdx:491 (439). Live measurement (extra/critic/toc.cjs, toc/toc.json): the tallest article pre on /curriculum/T3_Advanced/B-AXI-6_AXI_Verification_Performance/index is 18,600 px of a 72,186 px page. On the explicit-vs-implicit sub-page one pre is 10,536 px tall (extra/critic/out/gaps.json). 'grep -rln clipboard src' finds only src/components/ui/CodeBlock.tsx, which no MDX uses (theme-11), so lesson pre blocks have no copy button and no file or language label.
gaps.impact: A junior reader must scroll through 10-20 screens of monochrome code to reach the explanation that follows it. Experts who want the listing cannot copy it in one action. These full listings also break the on-page TOC tracking (gap-2) and make the lesson feel endless.
gaps.fix: Add a pre override (in the theme-11 rehype-pretty-code step) with a language label, a copy button, and, above about 40 lines, max-h about 28rem plus a 'Show all N lines' toggle. Port the clipboard code from ui/CodeBlock.tsx first.

gaps.title: Desktop 'On this page' never scrolls to follow the reader, so the active entry leaves the panel for the last third of long lessons
gaps.where: Right-hand TOC from xl (1280 px), every long lesson
gaps.evidence: [...slug]/page.tsx:125 makes the TOC column xl:sticky with xl:max-h-[calc(100vh-7rem)] and xl:overflow-y-auto. LessonToc.tsx:84-98 tracks activeId with an IntersectionObserver but never scrolls its own container (it has no scrollIntoView or scrollTop). Wheel-scroll probe on /curriculum/T3_Advanced/B-AXI-2_AXI_Burst_Math/index at 1440x900 (extra/critic/toc2.cjs; output in this task): the TOC box spans y 96-884 with scrollHeight 1484, and its scrollTop stays 0 for the whole page. From step 33 of 47 the active link sits at y 967-1658, below the box. Screenshot extra/critic/toc2/lesson-axi2.toc80.png shows no highlighted entry in view at 80% of the lesson.
gaps.impact: In the Push Further, Practice and References parts of every long lesson, the desktop reader loses the 'where am I' cue that the TOC exists to give. These are the expert-facing sections.
gaps.fix: In LessonToc, when activeId changes, scroll the active link into the nearest position inside the TOC container (a block:'nearest' scroll on that container only, instant under reduced motion). Pair it with layout-11's collapsible layer groups.
tests: tests/components/LessonToc.test.tsx (active entry scrolled into the container)
new Playwright check on B-AXI-2 at 1440: active link inside TOC box at 90% scroll

gaps.title: WaveDrom waveforms render on a fixed white panel with default blue signal names in every theme
gaps.where: /practice/waveform-studio and the 6 ProtocolWaveform embeds in 3 AMBA lesson files
gaps.evidence: src/components/practice/WaveformStudio.tsx:126 wraps the render in 'bg-white'. src/components/mdx/ProtocolWaveform.tsx:87 uses 'border-slate-200 bg-white ... shadow-slate-200/60'. extra/critic/out/waveform.default-dark.s0.png shows a bright white rectangle with #00f-style signal names inside the navy page. extra/critic/out/waveform.default-light.island0.png shows a pure black (#020617) WaveJSON textarea beside the same white panel on the cream page. 'grep -ro "<ProtocolWaveform" content | wc -l' gives 6.
gaps.impact: Waveforms are the core visual of the AMBA tier. In dark mode they are the brightest thing on the screen, glaring and pasted on, and their default skin ignores the site's signal colours.
gaps.fix: Render WaveDrom onto the code-surface token (the same always-dark panel as code) and restyle its SVG text, strokes and hatching through CSS variables scoped to the wrapper. Remove bg-white in both components.
tests: tests/e2e/theming.spec.ts (waveform panel background is not white in dark)

gaps.title: Header content is centred on the viewport while the page below is docked-sidebar plus column, so the logo, nav, breadcrumb and article never line up
gaps.where: All learning pages from lg (1024 px), most visible at 1440 and 1920
gaps.evidence: Navbar.tsx:521 has an inner 'mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 sm:px-6 lg:px-8', centred on the full viewport. MainLayout.tsx:22-23 centres a 'container' inside the area to the right of the 288 px outline. extra/critic/wide/lesson-f1a.w1920.png: the outline toggle and logo start at x of about 352, the outline at 0-288, the breadcrumb bar at 528-1680 and the article at 528-1392 (wide/wide.json). At 1440 (shots/lesson-f1a.desktop.default-dark.s0.png) the logo sits at x of about 112, over the outline panel, which has its own collapse button at x of about 259.
gaps.impact: The top of every page looks unaligned, and at wide sizes there is a dead band on both sides of the header. This is the main visual-structure cue that the shell was assembled from separate parts.
gaps.fix: Make the header full-width with a left slot equal to the outline width (w-72) when the outline is docked, so the logo sits over the outline and the nav and search start at the main column. Otherwise align the header container to MainLayout's container.
tests: a Playwright check at 1440 and 1920 that the logo's left edge equals the outline's content edge

gaps.title: One failing interactive takes down the whole lesson, and non-lesson routes have no error page at all
gaps.evidence: 'find src/app -name error.tsx -o -name global-error.tsx' finds only src/app/(learning)/curriculum/[...slug]/error.tsx. 'grep -rlnE "ErrorBoundary|getDerivedStateFromError" src' finds only ui/WebGLFallbackBoundary.tsx and ui/CodeEditor.tsx. So the about 118 interactives mounted through src/components/mdx/LazyMdxInteractive.tsx have no per-component boundary. A throw in one replaces the entire lesson (often 40,000+ px) with LessonError. On practice, lab and dashboard routes, a client error falls through to Next's unthemed default error screen with no navbar.
gaps.impact: Learner data lives in the browser and can be old or odd, and interactives are client code, so a single bad state can blank a 75-minute lesson or leave a learner on an unstyled dead end.
gaps.fix: Wrap each LazyMdxInteractive and VisualFrame in a small boundary that shows 'This interactive failed to load' plus a retry, inside its reserved height. Add src/app/(learning)/error.tsx reusing FindYourWayBack, and a minimal themed src/app/global-error.tsx.
tests: new tests/components/InteractiveBoundary.test.tsx (child throws, lesson text still renders)
tests/app (learning) error page renders navbar and ways back

gaps.title: In Windows forced-colours mode the primary button and fill-only selected states lose their boundaries
gaps.where: Every default Button (hero 'Find your level', primary CTAs), filled chips and tabs (dashboard sub-nav, interactive scenario chips)
gaps.evidence: src/components/ui/Button.tsx:14 default variant is 'btn-gradient text-primary-foreground' with no border. 'grep -rn forced-colors src' returns nothing. Playwright with forcedColors 'active' (extra/critic/wide.cjs): extra/critic/wide/home.forced.s0.png shows 'Find your level' as bare yellow text with no button shape beside an outlined 'Browse the curriculum'. Selected tabs such as 'Review' on /dashboard/review are shown only by a background fill (extra/critic/out/review.default-dark.s0.png), which forced colours removes.
gaps.impact: High-contrast users cannot tell the primary action is a button or which tab or chip is selected.
gaps.fix: Add border border-transparent to Button's default variant and to filled chip and tab styles, plus forced-colors:border-[ButtonText] and a forced-colors outline on selected states. Fold this into the theme-15 token work.
tests: a Playwright forced-colors smoke test on / and /dashboard/review

strengths: Interactives already follow the theme tokens: in default-light, the UVM phasing and RAL predictor interactives keep their semantic colours and readable panels (extra/critic/out/lesson-uvm-phasing.default-light.island1.png, lesson-ral-sub.default-light.island1.png). Keep this when the tokens change.

The course outline auto-scrolls to the current lesson (Sidebar.tsx:316-320), nests sub-lessons under their module, and the lesson header says 'Lesson 2 of 4 in A-UVM-4B · module 7 of 22' (extra/critic/out/lesson-ral-sub.default-light.s0.png). That is strong orientation for 112 lessons.
Lesson headings have scroll-mt-28 under the sticky navbar ([...slug]/page.tsx:134), and other anchor pages use scroll-mt-24, so in-page jumps are not hidden under the header.
Empty states are written for a first-time, no-login learner ('Nothing to review yet ... Browse the curriculum', extra/critic/out/review.default-dark.s0.png) and are labelled 'Saved in this browser'.
The 3D array sandbox degrades to a 2D view that shows the same state when WebGL is missing (extra/critic/out/sv3d.default-dark.s0.png, WebGLFallbackBoundary).
The 404 page wraps itself in the learning layout, so it is never a dead end (src/app/not-found.tsx). The lesson error page offers a retry and ways back.
The Expert index (716 expert topics in 74 of 74 modules, linked to the headings) is a distinctive asset for senior learners. It needs a better entry point (navigation-14), not a redesign.
'Deterministic educational model' plus 'Assumptions and limits' badges on practice tools state honestly what each model is.
notCovered: Viewport 2560x1080: every page returned an empty DOM in extra/critic/wide.cjs, most likely the intermittent 1102 Worker error (navigation-1), so ultra-wide layout above 1920 was not checked.
/dashboard/notebook and /dashboard/review were checked only empty. Populated states (many cards, long notes) need seeded learner-store data, which was not set up.
Theme switching while an interactive is mounted (do SVG or canvas visuals re-read the tokens without a reload) was not tested. It needs per-interactive interaction scripts.

Only 5 of 112 lessons were probed in the light theme (F1A, I-UVM-1C, B-AXI-2, the A-UVM-4B sub-page and E-DBG-1), and the other ~110 interactives were not each viewed in light and dark. A full per-interactive theme sweep needs a scripted run over the MDX registry.
The 11 practice visualization pages other than uvm-phasing and uvm-architecture, and 3 of 4 exercises, were loaded in metrics only or not at all, not visually reviewed.
Mobile and tablet views of the light theme beyond the lead's set (lesson-f1a and home) were not re-captured.
Keyboard focus-ring visibility on the cream default-light background was not measured separately. theme-15 covers ring tokens and responsive-a11y covers the keyboard walk in dark.
Screen-reader announcement of the TOC active state and of lazy interactives was not tested with real assistive technology.
The /community, /community/post/[postId] and /notifications routes exist in src/app but are not in the sitemap. They were not opened. navigation recommends deleting community/test-page.
